summary: Guard runFanout's per-entry setupWorktree hook so one entry's throw parks that entry instead of crashing the whole wave.

per.section: Every `.git/worktrees` mutation is serialized; the agent fanout is not

tests: a two-entry wave where one entry's setupWorktree hook throws still completes: the throwing entry is recorded in provisionFailures and stays pending, the other proceeds to runFanoutEntry
worktree/extraEnv indices stay aligned to the surviving entries after a sibling's hook failure is spliced out
acceptance: A setupWorktree hook throw on one entry of a multi-entry wave no longer crashes the tick; that entry is parked via provisionFailures exactly like a createWorktree failure, and siblings still ship.
notes: inbox 2026-08-03. chain.ts's setupBuildWorktree docstring (~L210-217) documents this gap as current fact; chain.ts is outside every phase lane, so updating that docstring once this ships is an operator follow-up, not part of this entry.

edit.description: add scopeWritesToEntry?: boolean (default false); correct entryChannelPaths doc to describe entry narrowing as opt-in, not automatic on every scoped tick
runAfterCommitGates passes the entry write-scope to writablePathsGate only when phase.scopeWritesToEntry is true; otherwise undefined, matching a singleton tick
prependHarnessBlock renders effectiveFenceLines only when phase.scopeWritesToEntry; otherwise unscopedFenceLines even with an assignedEntry

summary: Gate entry-scoped write narrowing behind Phase.scopeWritesToEntry (default false); dispatcher and prompt both respect it.

per.section: The entry-scoped write guard is opt-in, and off by default

tests: a scoped tick on a phase with scopeWritesToEntry undeclared writes with the same allowance and renders the same fence as a singleton tick (writablePaths ceiling only)
a scoped tick on a phase with scopeWritesToEntry: true narrows to entry.files ∪ entryChannelPaths under writablePaths and the prompt renders the two-fence block — unchanged from today's behavior
acceptance: Phase.scopeWritesToEntry (default false) governs both the write guard and the prompt fence identically; flume's own chain (which declares nothing) gets containment-only on every tick, scoped or not.
notes: Closes the two > **Drift:** notes in spec/pending.md and spec/prompt.md — one dispatcher ternary and one prompt fence choice, same mechanism. No .flume/chain.ts change needed; default false already matches flume's own expectation.

summary: Add behavioral test coverage for chain.ts's four load-bearing predicates: plan.shouldRun, plan.handoff, build.handoff, setupBuildWorktree.

per.section: Declining a tick before the invocation

tests: plan.shouldRun declines only when pending.json carries a pickable entry AND inbox.md is empty; runs on a non-empty inbox, a missing inbox.md, an empty queue, a parked-only queue, a live-blocked queue, a promotable-only queue, and undefined pending
plan.handoff's `Plan continues:` regex over state.md correctly drives re-wake vs handoff, including an absent line
build.handoff's wake condition, including the voluntary-bail leg
setupBuildWorktree's sentinel assertion throws when node_modules/<sentinel> is missing after install and passes when present
acceptance: The four predicates are driven through the real chain factory (loadChainModule + buildFlumeApi, as tests/examples.integration.test.ts already drives examples/), not a hand-copied reimplementation of chain.ts's logic.
notes: inbox 2026-08-02, narrowed to the four predicates only — chain.ts's declarations (writablePaths, gate lists, entry extension) are out of scope, same as CLAUDE.md itself. tests/** rides the channel; no files declared.

new.description: derive the [Unreleased] section from git log since the last release tag, per spec/cli.md Versioning policy

edit.description: add a script entry invoking the changelog tool

summary: Add a release-time tool that derives the [Unreleased] changelog section from git history since the last release tag.
tests: derives [Unreleased] content from the commit range since the last release tag, using build: commit subjects as entry tags and bodies as the why
a tag history that stops short of CHANGELOG.md's latest recorded version (tags at v0.6.2, CHANGELOG at 0.9.0) resolves via a defined fallback, not an assumption
a zero-commit range refuses loudly instead of emitting an empty [Unreleased] section
preserves the ### Breaking subheading convention for commits whose body marks a break
acceptance: Running the tool over real history produces a well-formed [Unreleased] section per spec/cli.md Versioning policy, and it refuses non-zero on a zero-commit range.
notes: inbox 2026-08-03, successor to the reverted .changeset/ fragment approach (e87c007). Ships the tool only; running it at an actual release cut is separate.
